english: Let $C$ be the curve given by $x=t\log_{e}t,\ y=t^{2}$, $t>0$. Let $P$ be the point on $C$ at which the tangent to $C$ passes through the origin $O$. The normal to $C$ at $P$ meets the $x$-axis at the point $N$. Then the area of the triangle $OPN$ is equal to
hindi: माना कि $C$ वक्र $x=t\log_{e}t,\ y=t^{2}$, $t>0$ द्वारा दिया गया है। माना कि $P$ वक्र $C$ पर वह बिन्दु है जिस पर $C$ की स्पर्श रेखा मूलबिन्दु $O$ से होकर जाती है। $P$ पर $C$ का अभिलम्ब $x$-अक्ष को बिन्दु $N$ पर मिलता है। तब त्रिभुज $OPN$ का क्षेत्रफल बराबर है
solution: At $t=1$ the point is $(0,1)$ and the tangent $y=2x+1$ misses $O$; for $t\neq1$, tangent through $O$ means slope $=\dfrac{y}{x}=\dfrac{t}{\log_{e}t}$
$\dfrac{2t}{1+\log_{e}t}=\dfrac{t}{\log_{e}t}\Rightarrow 2\log_{e}t=1+\log_{e}t\Rightarrow t=e$, so $P=(e,e^{2})$ and the tangent slope is $e$
solution_full: For the parametric curve, $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=\log_{e}t+1$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=2t$. Where $\log_{e}t+1\neq0$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{2t}{1+\log_{e}t}$. (At $t=\dfrac1e$ the tangent is the vertical line $x=-\dfrac1e$, which does not pass through $O$.)

The tangent at the point with parameter $t$ passes through $O$ exactly when the slope of $OP$ equals the slope of the tangent. At $t=1$ the point is $(0,1)$, where the tangent is $y=2x+1$; it does not pass through $O$. For $t\neq1$, $x\neq0$ and the slope of $OP$ is $\dfrac{y}{x}=\dfrac{t^{2}}{t\log_{e}t}=\dfrac{t}{\log_{e}t}$.
Equating: $\dfrac{2t}{1+\log_{e}t}=\dfrac{t}{\log_{e}t}$. Since $t>0$, cancel $t$: $2\log_{e}t=1+\log_{e}t$, so $\log_{e}t=1$ and $t=e$. Hence $P$ is unique: $P=(e\log_{e}e,\ e^{2})=(e,e^{2})$.
Slope of the tangent at $P$: $\dfrac{2e}{1+1}=e$ (the tangent is $y=ex$, which indeed passes through $O$). Slope of the normal: $-\dfrac1e$.
Triangle $OPN$ has base $ON=e+e^{3}$ on the $x$-axis and height equal to the ordinate of $P$, namely $e^{2}$. Area $=\dfrac12\left(e+e^{3}\right)e^{2}=\dfrac{e^{3}\left(1+e^{2}\right)}{2}$.
(A sign slip in the normal gives $N=(e-e^{3},0)$ and option (B); omitting the factor $\dfrac12$ gives (D).)
originality_note: New: the point is fixed by a transcendental tangency condition on an unusual parametrisation (x = t ln t, y = t^2), where the condition collapses to ln t = 1, and the normal then closes a triangle with the tangent through O (way 5). Closest known: 'tangent from the origin to y = e^x / y = ln x' and textbook normal-area exercises on standard parametric curves. Different because: the curve is not one of the known parametric skeletons, the condition y/x = dy/dx must be set up parametrically (with the t = 1 point excluded separately), and both tangent and normal are used.

concept_use.Parametric Differentiation: dy/dx = 2t/(1 + ln t) is obtained as (dy/dt)/(dx/dt); the tangency-through-origin condition is written with it.
concept_use.Tangent and normal for a parametrically: The tangent at P passes through O (fixes t = e) and the normal at P meets the x-axis at N, giving the triangle.

stem_review: Read as a student: every function has a stated domain, every symbol is introduced before use, every condition is given, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy/mpmath and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked that P is unique (ln t = 1 only; the t = 1 point (0,1) and the vertical tangent at t = 1/e do not pass through O), that 'area of triangle OPN' is unambiguous, and that only (C) equals e^3(1+e^2)/2; the distractors are the normal-intercept sign slip (B), a dropped factor e (A) and the missing 1/2 (D). Changed: the first two designs (a nodal cubic, then a normal-that-is-also-a-tangent on x = 3t^2, y = 2t^3) were replaced after the web check found near-identical published problems.
key_step: Writing 'tangent passes through O' as y/x = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) and solving 2 ln t = 1 + ln t.
justification: A routine chain of four parametric steps (slope, tangency condition, normal, area) with one light transcendental equation; no real insight, and options allow checking. Sits with the tangent/normal chain anchors 2026-P2-Q2 (L2) and 2023-P1-Q7 (L2).
blueprint_concepts: Tangent and normal for a parametrically defined curve
